To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and synthesized a class of solid protic ionic compounds based on imidazole or 1H-benzimidazole as base, and trifluoromethylsulfonic, nonfluorobutylsulfonic, para- toluenesulfonic or trifluoroacetyl acid as proton source.

a class of solid protic ionic materials was synthesized and investigated, which are thermally stable, display sensible proton conductivity under anhydrous and humid conditions, and may inspire the design of novel protic ionic solids.

a class of imide-based protic ionics were synthesized, and their ionic conductivity in the solid and liquid state was investigated, and a physico-mathematcal model of ion motion was developed to explain the electrical response of the ionic compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of ionic compounds that are liquid at room temperature, or solid up to high temperatures.

a new class of protic ionics based on imidazole (Im) and benzimidazole (BIm) as the base, and one of the following as the acid: trifluoromenthanesulfonic (CF3SO3H, TfOH), nonafluoropentanesulfonic (C2F5SO3H, NfOH) or para-toluenenesulfonic (CH3C6H4SO3H).
a class of protic ionics that are based on imidazole and benzimidazole, and their protonated form, and are capable of conducting protons in the solid state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protonic conduction properties of these ionic compounds are strongly dependent on the presence or absence of water, and on the nature of the anions, which in turn affect their thermal stability.
the proton-conducting properties of these materials are strongly influenced by the presence of water molecules, which may be adsorbed on the surface of the material, and/or absorbed within its bulk.
these materials are promising solid proton-conductors for fuel-cell applications. [on SciFinder(R)]
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple and robust method was developed to prepare a class of solid-state protic ionic materials that are capable to display sensible conductivity even under fully anhydroous conditions.

a simple and straightforward approach, based on the Brønsted reaction of imidazoles with strong acids, may lead to the preparation of a class of solid protic ionic compounds, which display enhanced proton conductivity under anhydrous as well as humid conditions, at temperatures as high as 200 °C.
the proton-conducting behavior of imidazolium and benzimidazolium-based ionic-compounds can be tuned by the nature of the constituent acid, the temperature and the presence of water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a large, polarizable, and flexible anion in a solid matrix, may facilitate proton conduction even in the fully-anhydrouse state.
the presence of a strong Brønsted-acid site, such as the one present in imidazole, is not sufficient for proton conduction to take place in the solid state.

the proton conductivity in solid protic ionic compounds is not only due to proton transfer between neighboring Brønsted acidic sites but also due to the presence of a proton transfer chain between non-acidic sites.
